program.checker_template: Evaluate ONE independent required condition against the SOURCE and EDITED images. No reference label, previous answers or optimization feedback is supplied. Return pass if the condition is satisfied, fail if it is not satisfied, or unknown if the evidence cannot establish an answer. Inspect only this saved condition, its criteria and binding. Report factual evidence and confidence (0..1 or null). A pass means satisfaction of THIS condition, not an overall edit label. Do not anticipate the optimizer's target. Missing evidence or transport/schema failures must not become a negative observation. The final overall label is computed by code; you never supply it.

d2: The node checks only whether a disc-like object remains recognizable as a DVD, so it can pass even when the requested edit is not complete. In the images, the black object at right becomes a white disc, but the original small rectangular item near the center is gone and a separate white disc appears there; the edit may have changed the wrong object or introduced an extra disc. Refine the binding to track the specific requested black DVD from source to output and assess whether that same object was recolored white, using location/shape correspondence rather than treating any white disc as proof. Keep identity preservation as a distinct criterion, and report uncertainty if the source object cannot confidently be identified as a DVD. The five consistent high-confidence passes indicate a criterion/binding blind spot, not transport or dependency failure; do not force a negative label from the reference alone.
d1: The binding is too broad: it treats any white disc in the edited image as the source DVD recolored, which explains the repeated high-confidence passes despite the aggregate disagreement. Track the specific source object through location, shape, and surrounding context, and assess whether that same object changed color; do not count a newly appearing white disc as progress if the source DVD is absent or a different object was altered. In these images, the source has a small rectangular item near center and a dark object at right, while the edit shows a white disc near center and a white disc at right; the traces do not establish which, if either, corresponds to the requested DVD. Keep object identity and color change as distinct evidence, and return uncertainty when correspondence or DVD identity cannot be established. Treat the consistent traces as a binding/criterion blind spot, not a transport or dependency failure; do not infer the answer from the reference label alone.
